items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Except for Berklee and a few other places.

Yeah, exactly, but it was not common, and it would have meant going to Berklee or some other thing. Now, when we say music program for us, it’s so different than saying it to the kids who just left the room, because they mean jazz. We mean [?]. We had Queens College, with a major in clarinet, the most hated instrument of all time. Did I say that? So, we didn’t have that. But I agree with you totally that when I see what these guys get, I’m jealous, because they do get it from A to Z. They have no holes in their…

last – what I leave them with, because that means editing and leaving out, giving up what you love and finding out what you do, microscopic – make a microscopic thing into an explosion, writing 80 exercises on it. I have this thing that – I got rid of it from Richie. Maybe it’s a disadvantage, but it’s also an advantage, the fact that we didn’t have it formalized.
